findings.title: Live payment API key hardcoded in source
findings.why: The pk_live_ key is committed with the code, so everyone with repo or image access can charge customers through the payment API. The leak happened at commit; reachability cannot lower it.
findings.fix: Read it at startup: CHARGE_API_KEY = os.environ["CHARGE_API_KEY"]; rotate the committed key at the provider.
findings.cite: CWE-798; OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures

findings.title: Request email interpolated into SQL with an f-string
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT id, name, email FROM customers WHERE email = '{email}'"
findings.why: payload['email'] (line 127) reaches the query text through find_customer (line 132); the only check is an '@' in the string, so any caller of POST /billing/run can send x@x' OR '1'='1 and bill another customer.
findings.fix: conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM customers WHERE email = ?", (email,)).fetchone()

findings.title: Mutable default list becomes Invoice.items and accumulates across billing runs
findings.why: run_billing calls build_invoice without adjustments (line 136); Invoice(items=adjustments) aliases the one shared default list (line 70) and line 83 appends to it, so every run bills the line items of all earlier runs in the process. Customers are overcharged on the default path.
findings.fix: adjustments: list[LineItem] | None = None, then Invoice(customer_id=customer_id, items=list(adjustments or []))
findings.cite: Python Tutorial, 'Default Argument Values'; Python Programming FAQ, 'Why are default values shared between objects?'

findings.title: Path traversal: ?file= joined to EXPORT_DIR without containment
findings.why: name comes from the query string and is only checked for a .csv suffix; ../../ segments or an absolute path (os.path.join drops the base) read any .csv the process can open. The docstring says the admin app authenticates requests, but no gate is visible in this file.
findings.fix: return send_from_directory(EXPORT_DIR, name, mimetype="text/csv")  # safe_join, 404 on escape
findings.cite: CWE-22; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control; Flask docs, send_from_directory

findings.title: N+1 query: one order_items SELECT per unbilled order
findings.evidence:
rows = conn.execute(
    "SELECT sku, quantity, unit_price_cents FROM order_items"
    " WHERE order_id = ?",
    (order["id"],),
findings.why: Runs on the POST /billing/run request path once per unbilled order; the number of orders per customer is unbounded, so request time grows with the backlog.
findings.fix: One query: SELECT o.id, i.sku, i.quantity, i.unit_price_cents FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id WHERE o.customer_id = ? AND o.status = 'unbilled'

findings.title: Charge sent without an idempotency key; a timed-out success is charged again
findings.why: If the 10 s timeout fires after the provider has taken the charge, charge_invoice returns None, the run answers 502 and the orders stay 'unbilled', so the next run charges the customer twice. Assumes the provider accepts an idempotency key, as most payment APIs do.
findings.fix: Send headers={..., "Idempotency-Key": f"invoice-{invoice.customer_id}-{min(invoice.order_ids)}"} (a key derived from the orders being billed), and record the charge attempt before calling.

findings.title: Charge failures swallowed by except Exception: pass
findings.why: On the money path, a network error, an HTTP error and a succeeded charge with an unexpected body all become an implicit None with no log, so failed and possibly-charged runs look the same.
findings.fix: except requests.RequestException as err: logger.exception("charge failed for customer %s", invoice.customer_id); raise ChargeError from err

findings.title: Leftover debug print of the invoice on the request path
findings.why: Runs on every POST /billing/run and writes the invoice to stdout outside the logger's levels and handlers; it holds SKUs, prices and an internal customer id, no secrets.
findings.fix: Delete it, or logger.debug("invoice built", extra={"customer_id": invoice.customer_id, "items": len(invoice.items)})

findings.title: Unused import json
findings.why: No runtime effect; reader cost only.

questions.question: charge_id comes from the payment API response and is put into a file name. Can the provider ever return a value containing '/' or '..'? If so, write_invoice_csv writes outside EXPORT_DIR.
